<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <meta name="color-scheme" content="light">
  <title>Black circle</title>
  <style>
    *, *::before, *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }
    body {
      min-height: 100vh;
      min-height: 100dvh;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      background: #fff;
    }
    svg {
      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 90vmin);
      height: auto;
    }
    @media (forced-colors: active) {
      circle { fill: CanvasText; }
    }
  </style>
  <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 2 2'%3E%3Ccircle cx='1' cy='1' r='1'/%3E%3C/svg%3E">
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <svg width="400" height="400" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
      <title id="circle-title">Black circle</title>
      <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200" fill="#000"/>
    </svg>
  </main>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
I didn't change `0.html` because it's already in good shape and I couldn't find anything that would clearly make it better. It's a single black circle, centered on the page, and it already:

- **Resizes with the screen:** it's never more than 400px wide or more than 90% of the screen's shorter side.
- **Stays centered on mobile:** it uses `100dvh`, so it stays centered when the browser's address bar shows or hides.
- **Works with screen readers:** it has `role="img"` and a `<title>` that screen readers announce.
- **Works in Windows high-contrast mode:** there's a rule for that mode (`forced-colors`) so the circle stays visible.
- **Has a matching tab icon:** a small black circle is built into the file, so it needs no extra request.

Anything more would be a matter of taste, not a fix:

1. **Dark mode:** show a white circle on a black page when the system uses dark mode.
2. **Less code:** replace the SVG with a `<div>` styled with `border-radius: 50%`.
3. **A description:** add a `<meta name="description">` tag for search results and link previews.

If you had a specific goal in mind, like different behaviour, a different look, animation or smaller file size, tell me and I'll make the change.
